mnemonics.title: Quick Recall Mnemonics
mnemonics.description: Simple memory hooks for tricky peripheral classifications and features.

items.title: Mnemonic 1: Dual Input/Output Devices
items.decryption:
These peripherals perform both input and output functions:
• M — Modem (modulates/demodulates signals)
• N — Network Interface Card (NIC - sends and receives data)
• T — Touchscreen (senses touch input and displays output)
• F — Fax Machine (scans/inputs and prints/outputs documents)

items.title: Mnemonic 2: Impact vs Non-Impact Printers
items.phrase: "D-D-B (Dot Matrix - Daisy Wheel - Band = Impact) vs L-I-T (Laser - Inkjet - Thermal = Non-Impact)"
items.decryption:
Impact printers strike a ribbon physically:
• Dot Matrix, Daisy Wheel, Band/Line.
Non-Impact printers do not strike:
• Laser, Inkjet, Thermal (which are quiet, fast, and use chemical/heat/nozzles).

items.title: Mnemonic 3: Optical Character/Mark Recognition
items.phrase: "O-M-R (Marks) vs O-C-R (Text Characters) vs M-I-C-R (Bank Cheques)"
items.decryption:
Differences in scanning tech:
• OMR — Marks (exam bubble sheets)
• OCR — Characters (converts printed images to editable text)
• MICR — Ink with Magnetism (cheques in banking; uses iron oxide ink)

flashcards.title: Active Recall Flashcards
flashcards.description: Hover or click to reveal the answers. Revisit these cards to build instant recall.

items.question: What is the primary difference between a trackball and a traditional mechanical mouse?
items.answer: In a trackball, the ball is situated on top/side and is rolled manually with fingers while the device remains stationary. In a mechanical mouse, the ball is at the bottom, and the entire device is moved across a surface.

items.question: What type of printer uses a drum coated with photosensitive material and toner powder?
items.answer: Laser Printer. It uses a laser beam to create an electrostatic image on a rotating photoreceptor drum, which attracts toner (dry powder) to be fused onto paper by heat.

items.question: Which keyboard key is referred to as a 'modifier key' or 'combination key'?
items.answer: Shift, Ctrl (Control), and Alt (Alternate). They do not perform any action alone; they modify the action of other keys when pressed in combination.

items.question: Touchscreen, Modem, and Sound Card fall under which peripheral classification?
items.answer: Both Input and Output Devices (Dual Devices).

traps.title: Common Exam Traps to Avoid
items: Trap 1: Confusing the category of Touchscreen. A touchscreen is a dual device (input via touch digitizer, output via display panel), whereas a touchpad (like on laptops) is purely an input device.

Trap 2: Assuming all scanners convert documents into editable text. Scanners convert documents into raster image formats (like PDF/JPEG). Conversion into editable text requires specialized OCR (Optical Character Recognition) software.
Trap 3: Misclassifying Plotters. A plotter is purely an output device used for high-quality vector drawings, blueprints, and engineering graphics. Do not confuse it with digitizer tablets (input).

Trap 4: Believing MICR reads handwriting. MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition) reads only pre-printed characters printed in special magnetic ink (iron oxide) using standard fonts like E-13B or CMC7, typically found at the bottom of bank cheques.

deepDive.title: Input & Output Devices Core Study Notes
deepDive.description: Review Input and Output Devices classification and tech details.

sections.title: 1. Input Peripherals & Technical Workings
sections.content:
Input devices translate physical real-world inputs (keystrokes, movements, scans, voice) into digital binary signals (0s and 1s) readable by the CPU.

A. Keyboard Architecture

  • QWERTY Layout: Standard 101/104-key layout. Features alphanumeric keys, control keys, and navigation keys.
  • Modifier Keys: Shift, Ctrl, Alt. These keys alter the default input of other keys.
  • Toggle Keys: Caps Lock, Num Lock, Scroll Lock. They switch the state of the keyboard on/off.
  • Function Keys: F1 to F12 keys perform specific application-defined shortcuts (e.g., F1 for Help, F5 for Refresh).

B. Pointing and Positioning Devices

  • Mouse: Can be mechanical (uses a ball), optical (uses an LED/laser and photodiode sensor to track surface movement), or wireless.
  • Trackball: Stationary pointing device where a ball on top is rotated with a thumb or fingers. Ideal for CAD systems and confined spaces.
  • Digitizer/Graphics Tablet: A flat surface used with a stylus (pen). It converts analog strokes into digital coordinates, popular for graphic design.
  • Light Pen: Light-sensitive wand used directly on CRT monitors to select menu options or draw. It does not work on standard LCD/LED screens.

C. Scanning & Character Recognition Technologies

  • Optical Mark Reader (OMR): Detects the presence or absence of a mark (e.g., pencil bubble on answer sheets) by measuring reflected light intensity.
  • Optical Character Recognition (OCR): Software that converts scanned bitmap images of text (typed or handwritten) into editable digital text.
  • Magnetic Ink Character Recognition (MICR): Used in banking. Reads magnetic characters pre-printed with iron oxide ink (magnetic ink) to check authenticity and speed up cheque processing.
  • Barcode Reader: Uses a laser beam to scan black-and-white parallel lines (barcodes) translating them into alphanumeric data.

sections.title: 2. Output Peripherals: Printers, Plotters, and Displays
sections.content:
Output devices translate digital binary signals from the computer into a format readable by humans (visual, print, sound).

A. Printers: Categorized by Technology

Printer Category Sub-types Working Principle Key Characteristics
Impact Printers
(Physical striking)		 Dot Matrix Printer (DMP) Pins strike an ink ribbon to print dots forming characters. Slow, noisy, low resolution, cheap operation. Useful for carbon copies (multi-part forms).
Daisy Wheel / Band Printer Solid fonts or metal bands strike the ribbon. Pre-formed characters. Cannot print graphics/images. Quiet noisy.
Non-Impact Printers
(No physical contact)		 Laser Printer Uses a laser beam, photoreceptor drum, electrostatic charge, and dry toner powder. High speed, excellent text quality, quiet operation, uses Page-at-a-time printing.
Inkjet Printer Sprays tiny droplets of liquid ink through micro-nozzles. Excellent color photos, higher cost per page, risk of ink clogging if unused.
Thermal Printer Uses heat on special heat-sensitive paper. No ink or toner needed. Used in POS receipts, ATM slips. Print fades over time.

B. Plotters

  • Plotter: A specialized vector output device that uses pens to draw continuous, high-precision lines. Used by engineers and architects to print blueprints, maps, and CAD graphics.

C. Monitors & Display Quality Metrics

  • Display Types: CRT (Cathode Ray Tube), LCD (Liquid Crystal Display - uses CCFL backlighting), LED (Light Emitting Diode - uses LED backlighting), and OLED (Organic LED - self-lighting pixels, providing true blacks).
  • Resolution: Measured in pixels (horizontal x vertical). Greater resolution means a sharper image.
  • Dot Pitch: The distance between pixels on a screen. A lower dot pitch means sharper images.
  • Refresh Rate: Measured in Hertz (Hz); the number of times per second the screen redraws the image. Higher rates reduce eye strain.

sections.title: 3. Dual-Function Peripherals & Device Interfaces
sections.content:
Peripherals that act as both input and output channels, along with their physical connection ports.

A. Dual Input-Output Devices

  • Touchscreen: Senses touch (input) and renders graphics (output) on the same screen.
  • Modem: Modulator-Demodulator. Sends digital data over analog lines (input/output).
  • Headset with Microphone: Microphone acts as input, speakers act as output.
  • Network Interface Card (NIC): Sends data packet frames out and receives incoming packets.

B. Connection Ports & Interfaces

  • USB (Universal Serial Bus): Standard hot-pluggable interface for keyboards, mice, printers.
  • VGA (Video Graphics Array): Older 15-pin analog video interface for monitors.
  • HDMI (High-Definition Multimedia Interface): Digital connector transmitting both high-definition video and audio.
  • Parallel Port: Traditionally used for older printers (Centronics interface).
  • Serial Port: Used for older mice and modems (COM ports).
